title: The Class Presentation
description: Your teacher, Mr. Kim, has assigned a five-minute presentation on any topic you choose. The class will laugh at anyone who messes up—that's what happened to Derek last month. You have two weeks to prepare.

choices.label: Practice until you can recite it backwards

outcomes.narration: You rehearse in front of your bathroom mirror, your stuffed animals, your confused cat. By presentation day, you know every word. When you finish, the class applauds. Mr. Kim gives you a gold star. 'Excellent preparation,' he says. You've earned this.

You practice, but it's hard to focus. On stage, you freeze mid-sentence. Your mind goes blank. But then you remember one key point and start again, slower. The class is kind. You make it through. It's not perfect, but it's yours.

No notes, no memorization—just you and your topic about dinosaurs. You ad-lib a story about a T-Rex who opens a restaurant, and the class loses it with laughter. Mr. Kim is impressed. 'Real performance talent,' he says. You've discovered something about yourself.

You try to freestyle about your favorite book series, but nothing comes out right. You stumble through half-finished sentences, and the class fidgets. The bell can't ring fast enough. Some lessons are learned the hard way.

choices.label: Fake being sick to avoid it entirely

outcomes.narration: You convince your mom you have a stomach ache. The presentation day passes, and someone else goes in your slot. You feel relief, but also shame. Your classmates who presented get extra credit. You have to watch them celebrate.
